questions.question: ______ tissue cells separate to form different types of permanent tissue.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meristem.**__

__
 
• **Permanent tissues are derived from meristematic tissue once they lose the ability to divide. **
 
• They are classified as simple and complex tissues.
 
• Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are three types of simple tissues.
 
 
• Parenchyma tissue is involved in photosynthesis, secretion, food storage, and other activities of plant life.
 
• Collenchyma tissue provides support, structure, mechanical strength, and flexibility to the petiole, leaf veins, and stem of young plants, allowing for easy bending without breakage.
 
• Sclerenchyma is one of the three types of ground, or fundamental, tissue in plants; the other two types are parenchyma (living thin-walled tissue) and collenchyma (living support tissue with irregular walls).
 
 
 
• Xylem is planted vascular tissue. It transports water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant and also provides physical support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Permanent tissues in a plant are those tissues that contain non-dividing cells.
 
 
• **The cells are also modified to perform specific functions in the plants. **
 
• The cells of the permanent tissue are derived from the meristematic tissue. 
 
• The permanent tissue cells are also fully differentiated. The cells are large and a definite shape and size.
 
• The metabolism that occurs in the cells of the permanent tissue is fairly at a lower rate.
 
• **The permanent tissue in plants mainly helps in providing support, protection as well as in photosynthesis and conduction of water, minerals, and nutrients. Permanent tissue cells may be living or dead.**

questions.question: Which of the following is present at the growing tips of stems and roots and increases the length of the stem and the root?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apical meristem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Apical meristem** is responsible for the active division of cells and is present at the tips of roots and shoots.
 
• It is located in the apical and axillary buds of plants.
 
• **Apical meristem** facilitates the longitudinal growth of the plant, contributing to the increase in length.
 
• Behind the root cap, the apical meristem comprises actively dividing cells essential for primary growth.
 
• Most cells produced by the apical meristem are added to the elongation region, enhancing growth in length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Intercalary meristem**
 
 
• Located near the nodes in some plants, the intercalary meristem aids in the growth of leaves and internodes.
 
 
 
• **Meristematic Tissue**
 
 
• Meristematic tissues are regions in plants where cells are continuously dividing, contributing to growth.

questions.question: Stratum germination is an example of which kind of epithelium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Columnar epithelium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Columnar epithelium consists of elongated and column-shaped cells.
 
• These cells are often involved in absorption and secretion functions.
 
• Columnar epithelium can be found lining the stomach, intestines, and respiratory tract.
 
• In some locations, they have cilia or microvilli to increase the surface area for absorption or to move substances along the surface.
 
• Stratum germination (or stratum basale) is typically a part of columnar epithelium in the skin where cell regeneration occurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cuboidal epithelium**

 
 
• These cells are cube-shaped and are often involved in secretion and absorption.
 
 
• **Ciliated epithelium**
 
 
• This type of epithelium has hair-like structures called cilia on the surface.
 
• Ciliated epithelium is found in the respiratory tract and fallopian tubes, helping to move particles or fluid over the epithelial surface.
 
 
 
• **Squamous epithelium**
 
 
• These cells are flat and scale-like and are often involved in diffusion and filtration processes.
 
• Squamous epithelium can be found in areas such as the alveoli of the lungs and the lining of blood vessels.

questions.question: Which of the following is the unit of nervous tissue?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Neuron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neuron** is the fundamental unit of the nervous system.
 
• It is responsible for transmitting **nerve impulses** throughout the body.
 
• Neurons are composed of three main parts: the **cell body**, **dendrites**, and **axon**.
 
• The **cell body** contains the nucleus and is responsible for maintaining the cell's health.
 
• **Dendrites** receive signals from other neurons and transmit them to the cell body.
 
• The **axon** transmits signals away from the cell body to other neurons, muscles, or glands.
 
• Neurons communicate through **synapses**, which are the junctions between neurons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Axon**__

 __
 
• An **axon** is a part of a neuron that conducts electrical impulses away from the neuron's cell body.
 
• It is essential for the **transmission of information** over long distances within the nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Ganglion**__
 __
 
• A **ganglion** is a collection of neuron cell bodies found outside the central nervous system.
 
• They act as relay points and help in **transmitting signals** from the peripheral nervous system to the central nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Cell Body**__
 
 
• The **cell body**, also known as the soma, is the part of a neuron that contains the nucleus.
 
• It is responsible for maintaining the neuron's health and metabolic functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is not muscle tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Areolar tissue**__.

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Areolar tissue** is a type of **connective tissue**.
 
• It is **found beneath the epithelial tissue of the skin**, **visceral organs** such as the stomach, trachea, the walls of the blood vessels, etc.
 
• Its matrix is made up of glycoproteins.
 
• It has** two types of fibers**: **white collagen fibers** made of collagen and **yellow elastic fibers **made of elastin.
 
• **Functions:**
 
 
• The tensile strength of collagen fibers and the elasticity of yellow fibers protect the various organs from mechanical injuries.
 
• This tissue also provides rapid diffusion of the materials and migration of wondering cells towards the areas of microbial infection and injured tissues.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Striated tissue, Cardiac tissue**, and **Unstriated tissue **are all **muscle tissues. **
 
• **Striated tissue:** 
 
 
• The Striated or skeletal muscles form about 40% of total body weight.
 
• Striated muscles shape the body and also release heat when they contract.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac tissue:**
 
 
• The Cardiac muscles are contractile tissues present only in the heart and in the wall of large veins which enter the heart.
 
• These muscle fibres are supplied with both central and autonomic nervous systems and are not under the will of the animal.
 
 
 
• **Unstriated tissue:**
 
 
• The Unstriated (Smooth) muscles are found in the posterior part of oesophagus, stomach, intestine, lungs, urinogenital tract, urinary bladder, blood vessels iris, ciliary body of eye, dermis of skin, etc.
 
• The Unstriated muscle consists of long, narrow, spindle-shaped fibres that are generally shorter than the Striated muscle fibres.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of meristematic tissues in plants?

options.text: Large vacuoles and thick cell walls
Absence of nucleus and presence of lignified walls
Actively dividing cells with dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
Dead cells that provide mechanical support

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Actively dividing cells with dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** consist of actively dividing cells that are responsible for plant growth.
 
• Cells in meristematic tissues have a **dense cytoplasm** and lack large vacuoles, which allows efficient division.
 
• These cells possess **prominent nuclei** to control cell division and metabolic activities.
 
• The cell walls in meristematic tissues are **thin and non-lignified**, facilitating flexibility during cell division.
 
• Meristematic tissues are located in specific regions such as **apical meristems, lateral meristems, and intercalary meristems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apical Meristems**: Found at the tips of roots and shoots, responsible for primary growth (increase in length).
 
• **Lateral Meristems**: Located in the sides of stems and roots, responsible for secondary growth (increase in thickness).
 
• **Intercalary Meristems**: Present at the base of leaves or internodes, aiding in regrowth of grass and other monocots.
 
• Meristematic cells lack **large vacuoles** because vacuoles are primarily used for storage, which is not needed during active division.
 
• Meristematic cells eventually differentiate into permanent tissues, which perform specific functions such as support, transport, or photosynthesis.

questions.question:
The cells of meristematic tissue have which of the following prominent features?

1. Dense cytoplasm

2. Thick cellulose walls

3. Intracellular spaces

4. Vacuoles

5. Prominent nuclei
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meristematic tissue cells are **undifferentiated and actively dividing**, which is crucial for plant growth.
 
• These cells are characterized by a **dense cytoplasm**, which supports high metabolic activity.
 
• They contain **prominent nuclei** to regulate cell division and growth-related activities.
 
• Meristematic cells lack vacuoles as vacuoles are mainly present in mature cells for storage and maintaining cell rigidity.
 
• These cells also have **thin cellulose walls** to enable frequent division and growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meristematic Tissue:** This tissue is responsible for the primary and secondary growth of plants. It is found in root tips, shoot tips, and lateral regions of stems and roots.
 
• **Types of Meristem:**
 
 
• **Apical Meristem:** Located at the tips of roots and shoots, it facilitates elongation and primary growth.
 
• **Lateral Meristem:** Contributes to the thickening of stems and roots (e.g., vascular cambium and cork cambium).
 
• **Intercalary Meristem:** Present at internodes or leaf bases, aiding in regrowth and elongation.
 
 
 
• **Absence of Vacuoles:** The lack of vacuoles allows meristematic cells to divide actively without interference from storage functions.
 
• **Cell Features:** Meristematic cells exhibit small, isodiametric shapes with dense protoplasm and are tightly packed without intercellular spaces.
 
• **Importance:** Meristematic tissue plays a key role in repairing damaged plant parts, producing new organs, and enabling overall growth and development.

questions.question: Which one among the following statements about epithelial tissue is correct?

options.text: Epithelial tissue forms a continuous sheet with tightly packed cells, having minimal intercellular spaces.
Simple squamous epithelium is found in the skin, lining of blood vessels, and lung alveoli, where transportation of substances occurs.
Stratified squamous epithelium is found in areas of absorption and secretion, such as the inner lining of the intestine.
Ciliated columnar epithelium are tall, pillar-like cells, is found in the respiratory tract, where its cilia help in filtering out the pollutants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1: __**Epithelial tissue forms a continuous sheet with tightly packed cells, having minimal intercellular spaces.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epithelial tissue forms a continuous sheet with tightly packed cells, having minimal intercellular spaces.**

 
 
• **This statement is correct.** Epithelial tissue is made up of **cells that are tightly packed together with very little intercellular space**__. These cells form a continuous sheet that covers and protects the body surfaces and organs. The minimal intercellular spaces ensure that the epithelium provides an effective barrier, regulating the passage of materials in and out of the body.
 
 
 
• **Simple squamous epithelium is found in the skin, lining of blood vessels, and lung alveoli, where transportation of substances occurs.**
 __
 
• **This statement is incorrect**. Simple squamous epithelium is indeed found in the lining of blood vessels and lung alveoli where the **exchange of gases occurs,**__ but it is not found in the skin. The skin is covered with stratified squamous epithelium, which is made up of multiple layers of cells to provide protection against wear and tear.
 
 
 
• **Stratified squamous epithelium is found in areas of absorption and secretion, such as the inner lining of the intestine.**
 __
 
• **This statement is incorrect.** Stratified squamous epithelium is primarily **found in areas subject to abrasion, such as the skin and the lining of the mouth or esophagus**__. The inner lining of the intestine is made up of columnar epithelium, which is specialized for absorption and secretion, not stratified squamous epithelium.
 
 
 
• **Ciliated columnar epithelium are tall, pillar-like cells, is found in the respiratory tract, where its cilia help in filtering out the pollutants.​**
 __
 
• **This statement is incorrect**. Ciliated columnar epithelium is found in the respiratory tract, where the cilia (hair-like projections on the epithelial cells) move in a coordinated manner to push mucus and trapped particles out of the airways, helping in cleaning the respiratory passages. They are **Cube-shaped cells.**__
 
 

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

**Types of Epithelial Tissue:**

 
• 
 
**Simple Squamous Epithelium**:

 
 
• 
 
Structure: Thin and flat cells that form a delicate lining.

 
 
• 
 
Location: Lining of blood vessels, lung alveoli, and oesophagus.

 
 
• 
 
Function: Allows transportation of substances across a selectively permeable surface.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Stratified Squamous Epithelium**:

 
 
• 
 
Structure: Cells are arranged in many layers.

 
 
• 
 
Location: Skin (to prevent wear and tear), lining of the mouth.

 
 
• 
 
Function: Protective layer.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Columnar Epithelium**:

 
 
• 
 
Structure: Tall, pillar-like cells.

 
 
• 
 
Location: Inner lining of the intestine.

 
 
• 
 
Function: Facilitates absorption and secretion.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Ciliated Columnar Epithelium**:

 
 
• 
 
Structure: Columnar epithelial cells with hair-like projections called cilia.

 
 
• 
 
Location: Respiratory tract.

 
 
• 
 
Function: Cilia move to push mucus forward, clearing it.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Cuboidal Epithelium**:

 
 
• 
 
Structure: Cube-shaped cells.

 
 
• 
 
Location: Lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands.

 
 
• 
 
Function: Provides mechanical support.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Glandular Epithelium**:

 
 
• 
 
Structure: Cells that are specialized to secrete substances.

 
 
• 
 
Function: Secretes substances at the epithelial surface, forming multicellular glands when a portion of the tissue folds inward.

questions.question: What is the role of the basement membrane in epithelial tissue?

options.text: It separates the epithelium from the underlying tissue.
It provides a pathway for nutrient exchange.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It separates the epithelium from the underlying tissue.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The basement membrane is a thin extracellular structure that separates epithelial tissue from the underlying connective tissue.
 
• It acts as a selective barrier, supporting the epithelium while allowing the exchange of nutrients and waste between epithelial cells and connective tissue.
 
• Composed of two layers: the basal lamina (produced by epithelial cells) and the reticular lamina (produced by connective tissue).
 
• It provides structural support to epithelial cells and anchors them to the underlying tissue.
 
• The basement membrane also plays an essential role in regulating cell behavior, including cell adhesion, migration, and differentiation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basal Lamina:**

 
 
• The basal lamina is a specialized layer of the basement membrane composed of collagen (type IV), laminin, and proteoglycans.
 
• It serves as a filtration barrier, ensuring selective permeability between tissues.
 
 
 
• **Role in Pathology:**
 
 
• Damage to the basement membrane is associated with conditions like cancer, fibrosis, and autoimmune disorders.
 
• In cancer, the invasion of epithelial cells through the basement membrane is a critical step in metastasis.
 
 
 
• **Cell Adhesion Molecules (CAMs):**
 
 
• CAMs like integrins play a crucial role in anchoring epithelial cells to the basement membrane.
 
• These molecules facilitate communication between the epithelium and connective tissue, influencing cellular responses.
 
 
 
• **Nutrient Exchange:**
 
 
• The basement membrane allows the diffusion of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products between epithelial cells and underlying connective tissues.
 
• This exchange supports the metabolic needs of epithelial cells, which lack direct blood supply.

questions.question: Which of the following animal tissues contain(s) flattened cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Squamous epithelium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Animal tissues that contain flattened cells are primarily found within the category of epithelial tissue.**
 
• **Epithelial Tissue: **This type of tissue forms sheets that cover the external surfaces of the body (like skin), line internal organs (like the lungs and intestines), and form glands.
 
• **Squamous Epithelium: **Within epithelial tissue, the specific type that contains flattened cells is called squamous epithelium. These cells are thin and flat, resembling scales.
 
• **Functions:** Squamous epithelium serves various functions depending on its location:
 
• **Protection:** It forms a protective barrier against abrasion, dehydration, and chemical injury. This is evident in the skin, where it acts as the outermost layer.
 
• **Diffusion:** In areas like the alveoli of the lungs and the walls of blood vessels, the thin, flat nature of squamous cells facilitates the rapid diffusion of gases (like oxygen and carbon dioxide) and other substances.
 
• **Filtration:** In the kidneys, squamous epithelium lines the structures involved in filtration of blood.
 
• **Locations:** Squamous epithelium is found in various locations throughout the body, including:
 
• **Skin:** The outermost layer of the epidermis.
 
• **Lungs:** Lining the alveoli for gas exchange.
 
• **Blood Vessels:** Forming the inner lining of blood vessels.
 
• **Kidneys: **Lining parts of the nephrons involved in filtration.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement about muscle tissue.

options.text: Muscle tissues are made up of cuboidal cells.
Microscopes reveal alternate light and dark bands in voluntary muscles.
Special contractile proteins are present in muscles.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Muscle tissues are made up of cuboidal cells.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muscle tissues** are not made up of **cuboidal cells**. Instead, they are composed of specialized elongated cells called **muscle fibers**, which are designed for contraction and movement.
 
• **Cuboidal cells** are epithelial cells, typically found in glands and ducts, where their primary function is secretion or absorption, not contraction.
 
• Muscle tissue is categorized into three types: **skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscle**, all of which have unique structural and functional features.
 
• **Skeletal muscle fibers** are long, cylindrical, and multinucleated, with alternating light and dark bands, indicating their striated nature.
 
• **Contractile proteins**, such as **actin and myosin**, are present in all muscle tissues and are responsible for the contraction and relaxation process.
 
• Muscle tissues are integral to various bodily functions, including **movement, posture maintenance, and internal organ functioning** like the heart and digestive system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The limbs have voluntary muscles**__

 __
 
• **Voluntary muscles**, also known as **skeletal muscles**, are under conscious control and are responsible for movements of the limbs and body.
 
• These muscles are connected to bones via **tendons** and work in pairs to perform movements like flexion and extension.
 
 
 
• **Microscopes reveal alternate light and dark bands in voluntary muscles**__
 __
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are striated, meaning they have alternating light (I-bands) and dark (A-bands) bands visible under a microscope, which are due to the arrangement of **actin and myosin filaments**.
 
• This striation is a key feature distinguishing skeletal muscles from smooth muscles, which lack this pattern.
 
 
 
• **Special contractile proteins are present in muscles**__
 
 
• Muscles contain **specialized contractile proteins** such as **actin** and **myosin**, which interact to produce contraction and generate force.
 
• Other associated proteins, like **tropomyosin** and **troponin**, help regulate the contraction process.

questions.question: The layer of cells which is present in between endodermis and vascular tissue:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option -3 Pericycle.

Key Points -**__

__
 
• The layer of cells which is present in between endodermis and vascular tissue is called pericycle.
 
• **The pericycle **is a thin layer of plant tissue located between the **endodermis and the phloem(vascular tissue)** in the root of a plant.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the plant's growth and development.
 
• In root tissues, the pericycle is involved in lateral root formation. When a plant must grow a new root, cells in the pericycle divide and differentiate, extending through the outer layers of tissue in the root to the soil, forming a lateral root.
 
• In addition, in woody plants, the pericycle can contribute to the formation of the vascular cambium, which is a layer of tissue that generates the secondary xylem and phloem, contributing to the thickening of the stem or root during secondary growth.
 
• The cells of the pericycle are generally small and without large vacuoles.

**Additional information-**__

 
• **Pith - **The pith is an area of tissue found in the centre of the stem or roots in many types of plants. It consists of soft, spongy parenchyma cells, which are involved in storage and transport.
 
• **The cortex** is the area of a plant stem or root between **the epidermis (outer layer) and the vascular tissue (the xylem and the phloem)**. It is composed of various types of tissues, primarily parenchyma cells, and plays important roles in the plant's functioning.
 
• **The exodermis** in plants is a layer or multiple layers of cells that form a protective sheath around the outside of roots, located beneath the epidermis. It develops from the outer cell layer of the cortex.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to phloem?

options.text: Phloem carries photosynthetic products from leaves to other plant parts.
Sieve tubes in phloem are made up of dead cells.
Companion cells of phloem have perforated walls.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• Statement 1:
 
• "Phloem carries photosynthetic products from leaves to other plant parts."
 
 
• This statement is accurate. Phloem is responsible for the transport of photosynthates (mainly sugars like sucrose) produced during photosynthesis in the leaves to other parts of the plant, including stems, roots, and fruits.
 
 
 
• Statement 2:
 
• "Sieve tubes in phloem are made up of dead cells."
 
 
• This statement is not correct. Sieve tubes in phloem are made up of living cells.
 
• Although they lack a nucleus and some organelles, they remain alive and functional for the transport of sugars and nutrients.
 
 
 
• Statement 3:
 
• "Companion cells of phloem have perforated walls."
 
 
• This statement is also inaccurate. Companion cells are living cells that support the sieve tubes, and they have thin cell walls but do not have perforated walls.
 
• Instead, they contain numerous plasmodesmata (small channels) that connect them to the sieve tube elements.
 
 
 
• Statement 4:
 
• "Phloem transport is uni-directional."
 
 
• This statement is not correct.
 
• Phloem transport is generally bi-directional.
 
• It can transport nutrients both upward and downward in the plant, depending on the plant’s needs and the growth stages.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement about complex permanent tissue.

options.text: Vascular bundles are a characteristic feature of complex tissues.
Complex tissue includes parenchyma and collenchyma.
There is more than one type of cell in a complex tissue.
Cells in a complex tissue work together to perform a common function.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Complex tissue includes parenchyma and collenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Complex permanent tissues are composed of more than one type of cell that work together to perform a specific function.
 
• The major types of complex tissues are xylem and phloem, which are involved in the transport of water, nutrients, and food.
 
• Vascular bundles, which are a characteristic feature of complex tissues, contain both xylem and phloem.
 
• Parenchyma and collenchyma are types of simple tissues, not complex tissues.
 
• Complex tissues are essential for the conduction of water, minerals, and food in plants, contributing to their overall growth and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem:**

 
 
• It is a type of complex tissue responsible for the transport of water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• Xylem is composed of different cell types, including tracheids, vessel elements, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibers.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• Phloem is another type of complex tissue that transports organic nutrients, particularly sucrose, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• Phloem is made up of sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibers.
 
 
 
• **Simple Tissues:**
 
 
• Simple tissues, such as parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma, are composed of one type of cell.
 
• They perform basic functions like storage, support, and photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Vascular Bundles:**
 
 
• These are strands of complex tissues (xylem and phloem) found in the stems, roots, and leaves of vascular plants.
 
• Vascular bundles facilitate the efficient transport of water, nutrients, and food throughout the plant.

questions.question: Which of the following is a complex vascular tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phloem**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phloem** is a complex vascular tissue in plants that is responsible for the transport of nutrients, primarily sugars, throughout the plant.
 
• It is one of the two main types of vascular tissues, the other being xylem, which transports water and minerals.
 
• The phloem consists of various specialized cells, including sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma.
 
• It plays a critical role in the process of translocation, which is the movement of organic compounds from the leaves to other parts of the plant where they are needed for growth and storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a type of simple permanent tissue that provides mechanical support to plants but is not involved in nutrient transport.
 
• **Parenchyma** is a type of simple permanent tissue involved in storage, photosynthesis, and tissue repair.
 
• **Collenchyma** is a type of simple permanent tissue that provides support and flexibility to plant organs.
 
• The term **complex tissue** refers to tissues that are made up of more than one type of cell and perform multiple functions, such as the phloem and xylem in vascular plants.
